title: Gnosticism and Spiritual Nourishment
english: When the soldiers pierced Christ's side with a spear, water mixed with blood flowed out, illustrating the story of those who were baptized in the cloud and the sea and received spiritual nourishment.
However, these individuals slipped up by eating with idolaters, and instead of committing fornication with the Midianite women, they rose up to play.

It is essential to consider someone else's conscience, not one's own, and to forgive those who are to be forgiven, as conscience is related to gnosis, but in this context, it refers to someone else's, so that one does not build up ignorance by imitating what one does not know, becoming contemptuous instead of magnanimous.
The new converts in Corinth did not know the proper way to pray and had not yet refined their approach to God, so they prayed and brought their petitions, but did so in an unseemly manner.
Men and women should approach God with modesty and propriety, as men are given boldness, while women are restrained by modesty for the sake of propriety.

The apostle Paul attempts to persuade his audience to think what is right by appealing to the natural law, which serves as a kind of judge of what is fitting for each person, and he grounds this argument in the creation story, where God makes man in His own image, as it is written, 'I made man in the image of God' (Genesis 1:27).

Therefore, the head of the man is Christ, who is the archetype as God, but according to the law of nature and likeness to us, and when He became man, although He is God, He calls Himself the son of man everywhere, although He has an ineffable birth from God the Father.

Consequently, the woman was also made in the image and likeness of man, that is, Adam, not a different species, but rather similar and like him, as Adam himself clearly confessed, saying, 'This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh' (Genesis 2:23).

Since some say that the Son is created, like the rest of creation, of which Christ is the head, for Christ is the head of every man, it is necessary to consider that the power of blasphemy does not only touch the theory about the Son, but will also pass over to the Father.

For if they say that the Son is generated and should be considered among the creatures, since He is the head of every man, how would He not be thought to be created and made in the same manner, and also the Father, if He is the head of the Son who has a substantial relationship with us, or with creatures?

As they themselves say, the head is naturally connected to the rest of the body in unity, so through the Son, the relationship with God and Father will also come to every man, and thus, the question arises as to the nature of the Son, and how He relates to creation.

If the Son is the head of every man, and the Father is the head of the Son, then it stands to reason that the Father is also connected to the Son, and through the Son, to every man, but how can this be, when it is clear that God transcends the nature of what has been made?
Or what shall we seek as the Creator of all things, according to the natural order of creation?
